# PART 1: Room-by-Room Packing Checklist + Declutter Tips

---

## General Packing Rules

- **Label every box** on the top AND one side: room name, contents summary, and priority (OPEN FIRST / SOON / LATER).
- **Use color-coded tape or stickers** per room (e.g., blue = kitchen, green = bedroom). Tell movers the system.
- **Number your boxes** and keep a running list in a note on your phone. If a box goes missing, you'll know.
- **Heavy items in small boxes, light items in big boxes.** Your back and your movers will thank you.
- **Pack a "Last Out / First In" box for every room** — the stuff you'll need immediately on both ends.

---

## Declutter Decision Framework

For every item, ask in this order:

1. **Have I used this in the last 12 months?** No → it goes.
2. **Would I buy this again today?** No → it goes.
3. **Am I keeping this out of guilt or obligation?** Yes → it goes.
4. **Does it cost less to replace than to move?** Yes → it probably goes.
5. **Is it sentimental AND irreplaceable?** Yes → it stays. Photograph sentimental items you can let go of.

**Disposal channels:** Facebook Marketplace, Craigslist, OfferUp, Buy Nothing groups (fastest for free stuff), Goodwill/Salvation Army donation pickup, 1-800-GOT-JUNK, or a curbside "FREE" pile.

---

## 🍳 KITCHEN
**Estimated time: 6–8 hours total (pack over 2–3 sessions)**
**Responsibility: J**

### Declutter First
- [ ] Expired food, spices older than 2 years, duplicate utensils
- [ ] Chipped or mismatched dishes, mugs you never use
- [ ] Gadgets used fewer than twice a year (waffle maker? bread machine?)
- [ ] Takeout menus, old sponges, worn towels
- [ ] Plastic containers without matching lids (toss them all — buy a fresh set in Oregon)

### Pack — Weeks 4–3 Out
- [ ] Specialty appliances (stand mixer, food processor, slow cooker)
- [ ] Bakeware, seasonal dishes, entertaining platters
- [ ] Cookbooks
- [ ] Extra pantry stock (donate what you won't use before the move)

### Pack — Week 2
- [ ] Most dishes, glasses, and silverware (keep 2 place settings out)
- [ ] Pots and pans except one skillet and one pot
- [ ] Small appliances except coffee maker and toaster
- [ ] Wrap glasses individually in packing paper; stand them upright in boxes, never flat

### Pack — Moving Day Morning
- [ ] Coffee maker, toaster, last 2 place settings, dish soap, paper towels
- [ ] Remaining food → cooler for the road or trash
- [ ] Clean and photograph the fridge, oven, and countertops

### Last Out / First In Box — Kitchen
- [ ] Paper plates, plastic utensils, 2 mugs
- [ ] Coffee maker + filters + coffee
- [ ] Dish soap, one towel, trash bags, paper towels
- [ ] Snacks for the first night
- [ ] Corkscrew / bottle opener (you'll want it)
- [ ] Pet bowls and one meal's worth of dog food

---

## 🛋️ LIVING ROOM / FAMILY ROOM
**Estimated time: 3–5 hours**
**Responsibility: J**

### Declutter First
- [ ] Old magazines, catalogs, junk mail piles
- [ ] DVDs, CDs, games you won't play again
- [ ] Worn throw pillows, blankets with holes
- [ ] Cables, chargers, remotes for devices you no longer own
- [ ] Decor you've been meaning to replace

### Pack — Weeks 3–2
- [ ] Books (small boxes — they get heavy fast, aim for under 30 lbs per box)
- [ ] Framed photos and wall art (use corner protectors or cardboard sandwiches)
- [ ] Board games, media, decorative objects
- [ ] Lamps — remove bulbs and shades, wrap shades separately

### Pack — Week 1
- [ ] Electronics — photograph cable setups before unplugging. Bag cables and label them. Keep original boxes if you have them.
- [ ] TV — original box is best. If not, use a TV box kit ($15–$25) or wrap in moving blankets.
- [ ] Curtains and rods
- [ ] Remaining throw pillows and blankets (use them as padding in boxes)

### Last Out / First In Box — Living Room
- [ ] Phone and laptop chargers
- [ ] Power strip
- [ ] Bluetooth speaker
- [ ] One cozy blanket
- [ ] TV remote (bag and label it)

---

## 🛏️ MASTER BEDROOM
**Estimated time: 3–4 hours**
**Responsibility: J (each person packs their own clothes and personal items)**

### Declutter First
- [ ] Clothes you haven't worn in a year — donate or sell
- [ ] Worn-out shoes, stretched-out socks, single gloves
- [ ] Old pillows (replace every 1–2 years anyway)
- [ ] Nightstand junk drawer contents

### Pack — Weeks 3–2
- [ ] Off-season clothes
- [ ] Extra bedding sets, decorative pillows
- [ ] Books, keepsakes, jewelry you don't wear daily
- [ ] **Wardrobe boxes** for hanging clothes — worth the $12–$15 each

### Pack — Week 1
- [ ] Most clothes, leaving out 7–10 days of outfits
- [ ] Shoes except daily pair
- [ ] Dressers can be moved with clothes inside if drawers are secured with stretch wrap — saves box space

### Pack — Moving Day Morning
- [ ] Strip the bed. Bag sheets and pillows in a large trash bag labeled "BED LINENS — OPEN FIRST"
- [ ] Last outfits, toiletries go in your suitcase (travels with you in the car)

### Last Out / First In Box — Bedroom
- [ ] One set of sheets, 2 pillows, one blanket
- [ ] Alarm clock or phone stand
- [ ] Phone charger (yes, another one — put one in every First In box)
- [ ] Sleep mask, earplugs, melatonin if you use it
- [ ] Pajamas and next-day outfits

---

## 🚿 BATHROOM(S)
**Estimated time: 1–2 hours per bathroom**
**Responsibility: M (main bath), P (second bath if applicable)**

### Declutter First
- [ ] Expired medications and supplements (many pharmacies take back meds)
- [ ] Nearly-empty bottles, samples you'll never use
- [ ] Old toothbrushes, razors, makeup older than 6–12 months
- [ ] Stained or threadbare towels

### Pack — Week 2
- [ ] Guest towels, spare supplies, extra toilet paper (or donate)
- [ ] Under-sink stock, cleaning supplies (seal lids with tape and bag them upright)
- [ ] Medicine cabinet contents except daily meds

### Pack — Moving Day Morning
- [ ] Toiletries → ziplock bag → suitcase
- [ ] Shower curtain, bath mat, last towels
- [ ] Clean the bathroom last

### Last Out / First In Box — Bathroom
- [ ] Toilet paper (put this on top — you will need it first)
- [ ] Hand soap, one bath towel and hand towel per person
- [ ] Toothbrushes, toothpaste, deodorant
- [ ] Shower curtain and rings (new place may not have one)
- [ ] Basic first-aid kit
- [ ] Daily medications

---

## 🏠 HOME OFFICE / DESK AREA
**Estimated time: 2–4 hours**
**Responsibility: M or P (whoever uses it most)**

### Declutter First
- [ ] Old paperwork — shred anything older than 7 years that isn't a legal document
- [ ] Dead pens, dried markers, random office supplies
- [ ] Old tech (recycle at Best Buy or Staples)
- [ ] Manuals for products you no longer own

### Pack — Week 2
- [ ] File boxes for important papers (label clearly — do not put in the truck, keep in the car)
- [ ] Desk supplies, printer, scanner
- [ ] Books and reference materials

### Pack — Week 1
- [ ] Computer — back up everything to cloud AND an external drive before packing
- [ ] Monitor, keyboard, peripherals — photograph cable setup
- [ ] Shred the last of the junk paper

### Last Out / First In Box — Office
- [ ] Laptop and charger
- [ ] One notebook, a pen
- [ ] USB drive with backup
- [ ] Important documents folder (this stays in the car)
- [ ] Wi-Fi router (you may need it at the new place before the install)

---

## 🧺 LAUNDRY / UTILITY ROOM
**Estimated time: 1–2 hours**
**Responsibility: P**

### Declutter First
- [ ] Old cleaning products, duplicate supplies
- [ ] Wire hangers (dry cleaners will take them back)
- [ ] Broken or unused tools

### Pack — Week 1
- [ ] Cleaning supplies (tape lids, bag upright, don't mix chemicals)
- [ ] Iron, ironing board, drying rack
- [ ] Tool kit — keep one basic set accessible for disassembling furniture
- [ ] Washer/dryer: run an empty cleaning cycle, disconnect hoses, let them dry. Secure the washer drum with transit bolts if you have them.

---

## 🏗️ GARAGE / STORAGE / ATTIC
**Estimated time: 4–8 hours (the black hole — start early)**
**Responsibility: J**

### Declutter First — Hardest Room, Do It First
- [ ] Anything you forgot was out here probably isn't essential
- [ ] Old paint (check local hazardous waste disposal — cannot go in a moving truck)
- [ ] Broken tools, duplicate garden tools
- [ ] Holiday decorations you never put up
- [ ] Sporting equipment nobody's touched in 2+ years
- [ ] Moving boxes from the last move

### Pack — Weeks 4–3
- [ ] Seasonal items and holiday decor you're keeping
- [ ] Camping and sports gear
- [ ] Labeled bins of keepsakes

### Pack — Week 2
- [ ] Tools (wrap sharp items, secure loose pieces)
- [ ] Lawn and garden (sell or donate the mower if it's not worth shipping — a new one may cost less than moving it)

### Hazmat Reminder
Movers cannot transport and you should not put in a moving truck:
- Gasoline, propane tanks, lighter fluid
- Paint, solvents, aerosols with flammable propellants
- Pesticides, pool chemicals
- Ammunition and fireworks
- Perishable food

Dispose of these properly or use them up before the move.

---

## 🐕 DOG AREA
**Estimated time: 1 hour**
**Responsibility: M**

### Declutter
- [ ] Worn-out toys, stained beds, chewed-up items
- [ ] Old medications or food past its date

### Pack — Week 1
- [ ] Extra toys, grooming supplies, spare leash
- [ ] Off-season dog gear (coat, booties)

### Keep Out Until Moving Day
- [ ] Current bed or blanket (familiar scent = comfort)
- [ ] Daily toys, bowls, leash, collar, harness
- [ ] Food and treats for the trip (pre-portion into daily bags)

---

# PART 2: 6–8 Week Reminder Calendar

Copy these into Google Calendar, Apple Reminders, or any app. Each entry includes a suggested day, title, and details. Set alerts for the morning of.

I've organized by week. Adjust dates to your actual move day (marked as **Day 0**).

---

| Day | Reminder Title | Details | Who |

## 🚗 MOVING DAY ESSENTIALS — Ohio → Oregon

**Keep this page and everything on it IN THE CAR, not on the truck.**

---

### 📂 DOCUMENTS POUCH *(M — pack night before, 15 min)*
- [ ] Driver's licenses and passports
- [ ] Vehicle title, registration, insurance cards
- [ ] Lease / closing docs (both homes)
- [ ] Moving contract, Bill of Lading, inventory sheet
- [ ] Vehicle shipping receipt and carrier phone number
- [ ] Dog: rabies certificate, vaccine records, microchip number, vet contact
- [ ] Medical prescriptions (copies for each person)
- [ ] Insurance policy numbers (renters, auto, health)
- [ ] Cash: $300–$500 for tips, tolls, emergencies
- [ ] Phone chargers (car + wall) for both phones

---

### 🧳 PERSONAL SUITCASES — one each *(J — pack night before, 20 min each)*
- [ ] 3–4 days of clothes + pajamas
- [ ] Toiletries in a ziplock (toothbrush, deodorant, shampoo, contacts, razor)
- [ ] Daily medications and vitamins
- [ ] Glasses / sunglasses
- [ ] Jacket or layers (mountain passes get cold)

---

### 🐕 DOG KIT *(M — pack night before, 15 min)*
- [ ] Leash, collar with new ID tag, harness
- [ ] Food pre-portioned in daily bags + treats
- [ ] Collapsible water bowl + water bottle
- [ ] Poop bags
- [ ] Medications and calming aids
- [ ] Favorite toy + familiar blanket or bed
- [ ] Crate or car barrier / seatbelt harness
- [ ] Paper towels and enzyme cleaner (accidents happen)
- [ ] Vet records folder (copy)

---

### 🛏️ FIRST-NIGHT BOX *(J — pack morning of, 15 min)*
- [ ] One set of sheets + 2 pillows + 1 blanket
- [ ] 2 bath towels + 2 hand towels
- [ ] Toilet paper (on top — non-negotiable)
- [ ] Hand soap, dish soap
- [ ] Paper plates, plastic utensils, 2 mugs
- [ ] Coffee maker + coffee + filters
- [ ] Phone chargers (yes, another set)
- [ ] Power strip
- [ ] Trash bags (3–4)
- [ ] Basic tool kit (screwdriver, pliers, box cutter, hammer)
- [ ] Flashlight or headlamp
- [ ] Snacks + water bottles for arrival night
- [ ] Bluetooth speaker (morale matters)
- [ ] First-aid kit + pain relievers

---

### 🧊 COOLER *(P — pack morning of, 10 min)*
- [ ] Water bottles and sports drinks
- [ ] Sandwiches, fruit, protein bars, cheese sticks
- [ ] Dog water (separate bottle, labeled)
- [ ] Any temperature-sensitive medications

---

### 🚗 CAR EMERGENCY KIT *(M — verify night before, 10 min)*
- [ ] Jumper cables or jump pack
- [ ] Tire gauge + fix-a-flat or spare tire/jack
- [ ] Flashlight + extra batteries
- [ ] Reflective triangle or flares
- [ ] Blanket
- [ ] Paper maps or downloaded offline maps (cell signal dies in rural stretches)

---

### ✅ BEFORE YOU DRIVE AWAY — FINAL CHECKS *(J — 15 min)*
- [ ] Final walk-through: every room, closet, cabinet, drawer, garage, mailbox, yard
- [ ] Photograph every room empty (date-stamped)
- [ ] Read and photograph utility meters
- [ ] Return keys and remotes — get written confirmation
- [ ] Bill of Lading signed and your copy is in the documents pouch

# Packing Supplies Shopping List — 2BR Apartment/House

---

## How to Estimate Your Box Count

A 2BR household typically needs **40–70 boxes** depending on how much you decluttered and how densely you pack. The list below assumes a moderate amount of stuff — a couple that cooks, reads, and has a normal amount of clothing and decor but already did a solid declutter pass.

If you're a minimalist, buy toward the low end. If you have a packed garage or a lot of books, buy toward the high end. Most suppliers let you return unused boxes, so overestimate slightly.

---

## 📦 BOXES

| Box Type | Size (approx.) | Qty | Use For | Est. Cost Each | Subtotal | Who |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Small (1.5 cu ft / 16x12x12) | Book box | 15–20 | Books, canned goods, heavy items, tools, small electronics | $1.50–$2.50 | $23–$50 | P |
| Medium (3.0 cu ft / 18x18x16) | Standard | 15–20 | Kitchen items, toys, shoes, small appliances, bathroom, office supplies | $2.50–$3.50 | $38–$70 | P |

# Printable Label Sheet — Avery 5160 Compatible

## Setup Instructions

**Label stock:** Avery 5160, 5260, or any compatible 1" x 2⅝" (30-per-sheet) label
**Printer:** Any inkjet or laser
**Software options (all free):**
- **Avery Design & Print** (avery.com/templates) — search template 5160, paste the text below into each cell
- **Google Docs** — use the Avery Label Merge add-on or Labelmaker add-on
- **Microsoft Word** — Mailings tab → Labels → select Avery 5160 → paste text into cells
- **Canva** — search "Avery 5160" and use a blank template

**Print tip:** Print one test page on regular paper first. Hold it up against the label sheet to check alignment before printing on the real labels.

---

## Sheet Layout

The Avery 5160 sheet has **3 columns × 10 rows = 30 labels per page**.

I recommend using the sheet as follows:

**Row 1 (labels 1–3): Color-code key — print once and tape to your packing wall**
**Rows 2–10 (labels 4–30): Actual box labels — print as many sheets as you need**

You'll want **2–3 sheets (54–81 labels)** to cover 40–70 boxes with some spares.

---

## ROW 1: COLOR-CODE KEY LABELS (print 1 sheet with these across the top row)

These three labels sit across the top of the first sheet. Cut them out and tape them to the wall, or keep one in your documents folder for movers.

### Label 1 (top-left): Rooms A–C

```
ROOM COLOR KEY (1/3)
🔴 RED    ★  Kitchen   KIT
🔵 BLUE   ●  Living Rm LIV
🟢 GREEN  ■  Master BR MBR
```

**Font:** Bold, 7pt for the header, 6.5pt for each line. Use a sans-serif font (Arial, Helvetica, Calibri).

### Label 2 (top-center): Rooms D–F

```
ROOM COLOR KEY (2/3)
🟡 YELLOW ▲  Office    OFC
🟠 ORANGE ◆  Bathroom  BTH
🟣 PURPLE ✕  Garage    GAR
```

**Font:** Same as Label 1.

### Label 3 (top-right): Priority + Owner Key

```
PRIORITY & OWNER KEY
☑ OPEN FIRST = unpack day 1
☑ SOON = unpack days 2–3
☑ LATER = unpack when ready
M=Me  P=Partner  J=Joint
```

**Font:** Bold header 7pt, body 6pt.

## ROWS 2–10: BOX LABELS

Each label is 1" × 2⅝". That's small, so every character matters. Here's the template for each label — optimized for the tight space.

### Template (copy into every cell from Row 2 onward)

CONTENTS:_______________
________________________
PRI: □1st □Soon □Later
OWN: □M □P □J  FRAG: □Y

**Font sizes:**
| Field | Size | Weight | Font |
|---|---|---|---|
| Box number (#____) | 9pt | Bold | Arial or Calibri |
| RM and SYM line | 7pt | Bold | Arial or Calibri |
| CONTENTS (2 lines) | 6.5pt | Regular | Arial or Calibri |
| PRI / OWN / FRAG line | 6pt | Regular | Arial or Calibri |

**Spacing:** Set line spacing to "Exactly 8pt" or "Single" with 0pt before/after paragraphs. This keeps all 5 lines within the 1" label height.

## Alternative: No Printer? No Problem.

If you don't want to print labels, here's the low-tech version that works just as well:

**Buy these instead (P — $15 total, 10 min at Walmart):**
- [ ] 1 pack of blank white sticker labels, 3×5 or 4×6 (Avery 5444 or similar) — $6
- [ ] 1 set of colored dot stickers, 1" round, 6 colors — $5
- [ ] 2 thick black Sharpie markers (Magnum size) — $4

**Process:**
1. Stick a **colored dot** on the top and right side of the box (matches room color).
2. Write the **box number, room name, and contents summary** on the white sticker label.
3. Circle the **priority** and **owner** initials.
4. Draw a big **⚠ FRAGILE** if it applies.
5. Stick the white label on the right side of the box, next to the dot.

This takes about 30 seconds per box and is completely readable by movers. Honestly, this is what most professional organizers recommend because it's faster than fiddling with a printer on packing day.
